MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

L2·N12761unmasked layer
This neuron is mainly a detector of the *absence* of a paragraph break — it is maximally suppressed by sentence-final punctuation immediately followed by a newline (".\n", "?\n"), while its (much weaker) positive side fires on word-completing subword fragments/final tokens inside a continuing sentence (e.g. "ino" in "Vino", "istry" in "Dentistry", "." closing a quoted title).

L11·N1701unmasked layer
This neuron gives mild positive activation on ordinary function-word continuations inside grammatically fluent prose (e.g. " you", "It", " and", " no", " a", or the next sub-word of a proper name like "Madame T|ussauds"), and is strongly suppressed by keyword-stuffed SEO/spam text (chains of stacked search terms like "home ideas magazine uk", "Www mathematical soccer predictions", "Apa format psychology paper example professional writers") — i.e. it tracks natural-prose vs. keyword-list context rather than a single lexical item.
